result.title: STAR: Counterfactual Dual-World Rollouts and Spatial Target Adaptive Reconstruction for Visual On-Policy Distillation
result.summary: Vision-language models often rely on global context and language priors while overlooking answer-determining local details. Privileged visual on-policy self-distillation supervises full-image student rollouts using a frozen teacher that views high-resolution evidence crops. Yet our cross-scale diagnostics show that models retain over half of their full-image accuracy when local evidence is completely masked, indicating that single-image correctness does not guarantee reliance on local evidence, while the need for visual correction also varies across tokens with their spatial attention states. We propose STAR, a visual on-policy self-distillation framework combining independent counterfactual dual-world rollouts with spatial-attention-guided target reconstruction. Local image editing constructs paired worlds with identical questions and backgrounds but distinct answer-determining facts, where a shared student samples trajectories independently to expose contextual shortcuts under image-consistent prefixes. Within each world, the teacher contrasts real and mean-color crops to determine the visual correction direction, while the divergence between student image attention and a teacher-centroid spatial reference adaptively controls token-wise target log-probability reconstruction. Without auxiliary attention losses or test-time tool overhead, STAR improves Qwen3.5 across scales by up to 8.04 percentage points in average accuracy over initialization across six fine-grained benchmarks, reaches OPSD's final accuracy $4.7\times$ faster, and generalizes to out-of-domain reasoning tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断出 VLM 即使遮蔽局部证据仍能保持较高准确率，并提出 STAR：用局部图像编辑构造反事实双世界 rollout，结合教师对比真实与均值色裁剪的校正方向，以及按学生—教师空间注意力差异自适应重建 token 级目标，实现视觉 on-policy 自蒸馏。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「图像正确不等于依赖局部证据」的诊断与反事实配对监督，直接关联视觉证据是否真正参与答案、视觉旁路及贡献分配问题；注意力差异驱动的 token 级校正可供核查其是否促进证据使用，但该工作属训练期蒸馏而非 latent 推理状态生成。
